sentences.text:
Sanddp Rajak vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 November,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:55924
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Devnarayan Mishra

On The 7 th Of November, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 36867 of 2025
 Sandeep Rajak
 Versus
 State Of Madhya Pradesh And Another
 Appearance:
 Shri Sharad Verma - Advocate for the applicant.
 Ms. Neetu Pashine - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/S
 Order

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.632/2025 registered at Police Station Kolgavan, District Satna, for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(2), 376(2) (N),
506 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 5 read with Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The applicant is in jail since 23.06.2025.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
At the time of incident, the victim was a major and married woman.
After the applicant's marriage with another woman, the victim has lodged an FIR against him on 25.05.2024.

It is alleged that first time on 13.06.2022, the applicant committed sexual assault upon the victim and time and again, sexual assault NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55924 2 MCRC-36867-2025 was being committed upon her.
According to him, the applicant never approached the victim, but she herself visited the places as instructed by the applicant.
The victim was married on 10.12.2024.

It is also alleged against the applicant that he had taken the victim's nude photographs and sent them to her and her father's mobile whereas according to learned counsel for the applicant, no photographs have been recovered from the mobiles of applicant, victim and her father.
The applicant is aged about 21 years.
Trial will take time to be concluded, hence, the applicant be enlarged on bail.
3. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and has submitted that no case of bail is made out.

4. Heard the parties and perused the case diary.

sentences.text:
5. Considering the facts and circumstances brought on record, coupled with the facts that the incident started from 2022 and continued up to 2024 and that trial will take time to be concluded,
this Court deems it appropriate to allow the application.
Thus, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during pendency of trial.
7. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of BNSS.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55924 3 MCRC-36867-2025 8.
Accordingly, Misc. Criminal Case stands disposed of.
